description.value: The study examined neural responses to social inclusion, exclusion, and passive watching in females with borderline personality disorder, major depressive disorder, and healthy controls using the cyberball paradigm during fMRI.

spans.text: To examine social interactions under laboratory settings during fMRI and to warrant comparability with previous investigations, we used the well-established “cyberball” paradigm ( 20 ).

design.value: A 3 × 3 group-by-condition fMRI design compared healthy controls, borderline personality disorder, and major depression across passive watching, inclusion, and exclusion conditions, with scanner type and age included as covariates in further analyses.

spans.text: For second level group analyses, we computed a 3 × 3 ANOVA model (omnibus F -test) with the two factors “group” (HC, BPD, MD) and “condition” (passive watching, inclusion, exclusion) that included first level contrasts for the three ball tossing conditions for each of the three groups.

task_description.value: Participants took part in a virtual ball-tossing game with two other supposed participants; in reality, the game was computer-controlled.

spans.text: Participants were instructed to take part in the virtual ball-tossing game with two other participants that were supposed to be in another room. In fact, participants played against the computer and all actions were pre-programmed ( 2, 20 ).
The tasks consisted of three different conditions (“inclusion,” “exclusion,” and “passive watching” condition), each condition was applied once, each lasting around 2 min (60 throws).

stimuli.value: Participants were represented by a hand at the bottom part of a screen, while the other players were represented by animated comic figures.
